text: Alex 10-11: adopt godot-mcp-toolkit (NPGameDev) via a builder spike on its own branch, merge when ready; Godot upgrades are fine whenever. Bakeoff Ludo vs Bake3D ($10-15) after fixtures round 2 lands, on the cuff-blade strike and a quadruped beast. AssetFurnace skipped (16 GB Mac; cost isn't the limiting factor).
For the Ludo vs Bake3D bakeoff (after fixtures round 2): make a Bake3D account (email link sign-in) and buy the $10 Starter or $25 Maker pack; Claude can't create accounts.

10-11 Bake3D iron_knight.glb (~/Downloads/bak3d): 150k tris, 28 MB, rigged with 51 named bones (horse thigh/shin/foot L0/R0 front, L1/R1 hind, tail0-3, riderPelvis/Torso/arms, lance, motion_root), no animations exported. Our own procedural clips written in code on that skeleton (gallop, rear+strike, idle, fall) deform cleanly; lab is scratch knight/lab.gd. Battles use static MultiMesh pose meshes…
Alex 10-11: Bake3D model quality is far better than Ludo's, so the Ludo vs Bake3D bakeoff is dropped; Bake3D's own animations are weak, so we animate its rigs ourselves.

Alex 10-11: one rigged Bake3D model per unit, animated by our own clips, is the future-state art pipeline; Ludo stays while testing; invest cash and time once the game is proven fun. Lab, costs (~$300 Bake3D for ~65 models, 10-15 builder sessions) and plan live in tools/rig_lab/README.md (PR #212).
